transcripts.transcript:
Good afternoon, private banking, Rachel Tan speaking. How can I help you today?

Hi Rachel, Adrian Lim here. Got a break between appointments, so calling while the office is quiet. I've got my particulars ready also. My NRIC is S seven four nine nine six seven nine X. My date of birth is 4 September 1975.

Thank you, Adrian. I understand your objective is to reduce corporate credit exposure and free up part of your invested wealth for upcoming personal spending. We can keep our discussion concise. Are you somewhere comfortable to speak?

Can, meeting room empty now. Usually the phone keeps ringing outside, but in here quite peaceful. Been a busy day already; even my garden gets more attention than my lunch these days.

It sounds like the garden is keeping you occupied as well. Have you been enjoying it?

Enjoying it lah. Got herbs growing near the kitchen, and I check on them before leaving for work. Some mornings I get carried away, then realise the driver waiting already. At least it's a change from looking at emails.

That sounds like a pleasant change of pace. For routine portfolio calls, would you prefer that I arrange a time by message rather than call unexpectedly?

Message first would be better ah. My appointments move around, so a fixed slot quite difficult. If you send a message, I can find somewhere private instead of trying to talk while walking through the office.

I can contact you to arrange a convenient time for routine discussions. For today's call, please take a moment to bring up the portfolio screen.

Got it open already. Looking at my portfolio now, I've got Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031 here. Also got Nova Technology Equity Fund listed here. The screen a bit cramped on my phone, but I can read the entries.

Take your time with the screen. I'm here when you're ready.

For this transaction, use the holding I mentioned first lah, not the later one. I want to sell from my existing holding.

I recommend selling Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031.

Something to consider. Got the page properly displayed now; earlier the office connection a bit slow. You can carry on with the explanation.

For Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031, a deterioration in the issuer's creditworthiness could push down the resale price. Limited market liquidity also means your order could remain unexecuted if buyers will not meet your limit. You could lose some or all of the capital invested in this holding, and selling below your original purchase cost would realise a capital loss. Do you understand that weaker issuer credit could lower the bond's resale price, and that a lack of buyers at your limit could leave the order unexecuted?

Yes, I understand. Issuer credit gets worse, the price can drop; no buyers at my limit, the order won't get done. Still quiet here, no interruption from outside.

The transaction charge is 0.25%.

Let me refer to my notes ah. Got everything on the desk beside me. For the transaction currency, use US dollars. The amount for this transaction is 75,000. Quantity, put 250 units. Use a limit order, with the limit price at 300 American dollars.

Your final instruction is to sell 250 units of Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031, with a transaction amount of 75,000 in US dollars, using a limit order at 300 American dollars. Do you explicitly authorise this instruction?

Hmm, let me think a bit first ah, got a work message coming in.

Of course. We can leave the discussion here while you attend to that. You can contact me when you have time to continue.

Better leave it here first lah. Looks like they need me back in the meeting. I'll get in touch when I'm free. Thanks for your time, Rachel.

You're welcome, Adrian. Thank you for calling, and enjoy the rest of your day.
